Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - stakeholder mapping and procurement

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

- Stakeholder mapping (as I have it):
  * Economic buyer: Alex Taylor (CFO) - final sign-off on budget
  * Decision maker / product sponsor: Jordan Smith (CPO) - product fit & requirements
  * Procurement: procurement@enterprisecorp.com - PO and vendor onboarding
  * Security/legal: security.lead@enterprisecorp.com - questionnaire and SOC2

- Customer decision criteria we heard: cost per 1k tokens, predictable latency for synchronous endpoints, and clear data residency and retention terms.

- Immediate asks / next steps:
  1) Jordan - can you confirm the economic buyer and procurement contact emails? Also let me know if there are any internal timelines for procurement (e.g., next vendor review meeting).
  2) I'll share our SOC2 evidence and a draft SOW/pricing. If procurement requires a vendor form, we'll fill it and coordinate legal redlines.
  3) If budget is tight, we may need to request a buying-process exception (discount or SLA terms). I'll loop internal approvals once we have concrete numbers.

Attaching call notes and preliminary pricing for reference.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

- Procurement requires: completed vendor form, a copy of SOC2 Type II, and our legal team will review standard T&Cs (expect redlines).

Subject: Internal: Requesting buying-process exception for Enterprisecorp (DEAL-4581)

Hi Rachel / Nikhil,

Following the discovery call with Enterprisecorp (Jordan & Alex), procurement timeline is tight - they need materials by 2027-03-24 to hit their 3/30 committee. There's risk on the pricing front: Alex will escalate discounts >10% to C-level.

Deal summary:
- ACV (expected): ~$420k ARR first year
- Primary asks from customer: predictable latency for synchronous endpoints and a 99.95% uptime SLA with service credits (they may push for higher).

Requesting internal approvals to make the following exception offers if needed to close the deal this quarter:
1) Discount: up to 15% one-year contract (we'd prefer to cap at 12%).
2) SLA: allow 99.9% (standard is 99.95%) with defined service-credit schedule; legal may need to accept limited liability clause.

Attachments: pricing sheet and proposed redlines for T&Cs.

Can you confirm what discount % we can approve at your level and whether we can offer the SLA exception (or if VP/CRO sign-off is needed)? Time-sensitive - procurement deadline Monday EOD.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270322-pricing-sheet.xlsx, redlines_enterprisecorp_v1.docx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-22T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Requesting buying-process exception for Enterprisecorp (DEAL-4581)

Marissa - thanks for the clear ask.

I'm comfortable approving a commercial exception up to 12% for a one-year term (given ACV and strategic value). Please do not exceed 12% without CRO sign-off.

On SLA: we should avoid making custom SLA commitments beyond our standard 99.95% unless legal signs off. For procurement urgency, offer the standard SLA and propose a one-time Technical Review call with our SRE lead to discuss latency guarantees. If the customer insists on 99.9% instead of 99.95%, that's acceptable (less strict) but if they're asking for better than our standard we must escalate.

Next steps: Marissa, present the 12% discount option and standard SLA + SRE review to the customer. Loop me if Alex requests anything beyond that (e.g., liability caps).

-Rachel
VP, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
